payload.abstract: SemEval (Semantic Evaluation) is an ongoing series of evaluations of computational semantic analysis systems, organized under the umbrella of SIGLEX, the Special Interest Group on the Lexicon of the Association for Computational Linguistics. This project describes "Analysis of Clinical Text" task of the International Workshop on Semantic Evaluation 2014 and 2015 (SemEval 2014 and 2015) [2,3,4,5]. The purpose of the task is to enhance current research in natural language processing (NLP) methods used in the clinical domain, and to introduce clinical text processing to the broader NLP community. The task aims to combine supervised methods for text analysis with unsupervised approaches for entity/acronym/abbreviation recognition and mapping to Unified Medical Language System (UMLS) Concept Unique Identifiers (CUIs). It also evaluated systems on the task of template filling [1], which involves the population of eight attributes of the identified disorders with their normalized values.
